cell.label: Basic evaluation for UI: • History (eg, risk factor assessment and bladder record/diary/severity index/3-item questionnaire, minimum data set) • Physical examination • Measure postvoid residual volume • Urinalysis.
Recurrent symptoms and unidentified causes should be further evaluated.

Options: -Bladder ultrasound -Radiography -Urodynamic tests () Urge and stress UI • Simple cystometry • Office stress testing • Multichannel or subtracted cystometrogram. Overflow UI • Voiding multichannel or subtracted cystometrogram • Pressure flow study • Uroflowmetry • Leak-point pressures and urethral pressure profiles • Electromyography.
Evaluate and treat reversible or transient conditions.

Transient causes (DIAPPERS): Delirium or confusional states • Infections of the urinary tract • Atrophic vaginitis or urethritis • Pharmaceuticals • Diuretics • Sedatives, anxiolytics, and alcohol • Beta-adrenergic blockers • Angiotensin-converting-enzyme inhibitors • Antidepressive and antipsychotic drugs • Psychological conditions (eg, depression) • Endocrine disorder (eg, hypercalcemia, hyperglycemia) • Restricted mobility, urinary retention • Stool (fecal impaction).
